Good, my edit landed cleanly. Both files are in solid shape. Let me write my round summary.

This round I closed two real gaps in core view-model coverage that had sat untested since the earliest UI rounds:

`SessionEngineTests.swift` — the review flow's actual view-model, and after `SM2Engine` itself the next-most-important correctness surface in this app: grading advancement, again-rate math, and the locked per-deck attribution rule for mixed all-decks sessions (DEC-initial_discussion-005). Covers init states, queue advancement, again-rate over real vs. zero grades, per-deck stats attribution and ordering, elapsed-time via an injected mutable clock (no wall-clock dependency), and — this is the one I'd flag as most valuable — the `GradeRecorder`-throws error path: a corrupted card with no deck must set `saveError`, *not* advance the index, and clear cleanly on a successful retry. That's the actual mechanics behind "quitting mid-session loses nothing," not just the happy path.

`StatsMetricsTests.swift` — forecast/history/retention, empty and sparse on purpose since that's priority #3 in this whole project. While writing it I found a real, unfixed inconsistency: `dueForecast` skips any card with a negative day-offset, meaning an **overdue** card gets silently dropped from the forecast entirely instead of counting in today's bucket — inconsistent with `DueComputation.isDue` (what `DueQueryService` uses for the Decks badge), which correctly treats an overdue card as due today. That's exactly the cross-surface "due" disagreement DEC-initial_discussion-004 was written to prevent. I didn't touch `StatsMetrics.swift` — that's primary_ui's file — but I didn't write a test asserting the bug as correct either; I split it into a genuine future-exclusion test plus an `XCTExpectFailure`-documented defect test, so it's visible and precise rather than silently baked into "passing" coverage.

Same standing caveat on all of this: no `swift`/`xcodebuild` execution available to me here, hand-traced against the real source. Left for the integrator/Claude A: the `dueForecast` overdue-card gap is a real, specific, one-line-fix-sized bug (bucket negative-offset cards into day 0 instead of skipping them) whenever `Screens/Stats/` gets touched next — and still waiting on that first confirmed `xcodebuild test` run to know where all of this actually stands.
